text.p: Aquarius Exploration NL said on Monday it had secured finance for construction and development of the Kroondal platinum project in South Africa.

Aquarius said the two part mandate with investment bank Rothschild Australia Ltd was worth US$35 million and would be finalised following the completion of a bankable feasibility study, scheduled for early 1997, and the decision to mine.
The financing consists of a project loan facility up to US$20 million with a hedging facility of up to US$15 million.
The Aquarius project is located in the Bushveld Complex and settlement procedures for the three properties covering the project had recently been initiated, the company said.

After paying A$3.5 million cash and issuing 44 million shares and 44 million options for the properties, Aquarius said it had received an independent valuation on the properties of A$35.6 million with identified resources of 4.054 million ounces of platinum group metals (PGM).
The company said it planned an underground mine to produce one million tonnes per annum of primary PGM ore, commencing in mid-1998.
South Africa produces 68 percent of the world's platinum group minerals production of 4.98 million ounces.
By 2.45 p.m. (0345 GMT), Aquarius shares were steady at 15.5 cents on turnover of 330,000 shares.
